correctness.rationale: Use exact σ**(p^a)=(Σ_{j=0}^a p^j)-1_(a even) p^(a/2). For n=p^a, 1<H5<2; n=1 gives 1. For odd p<q, evenness of each divisor sum and coprimality with its base force Fp(a)=2q^v and Fq(b)=2p^u and an odd integer H5 strictly between1 and4, hence H5=3, p=3. The coprime factors of F3(2m) require m=1, q^b=5, yielding45. For n=2^a q^b, F2(a)=q^j while Fq(b) must be a power of2. The local lemma rules out all b>=2 for odd q, so b=1, q+1 power2 and F2(a)=q; inequalities force q=2^(a+1)-1, a odd; primality forces a+1=2, hence n=6. Direct fractions check H5(1)=1,H5(6)=2,H5(45)=3; independent bounded two-prime exponent enumeration found no further witnesses.
residual_risks: Bounded exponent checks support but cannot replace the all-a,b local lemma proof.

value.rationale: The H5 quotient is a natural divisor-theoretic variant introduced by Sándor. Completing the entire first two prime-support strata with arbitrary exponents and proving exclusion by a nontrivial local power-of-two obstruction resolves more than a small tabular lookup or a mere renaming of the unitary harmonic theorem.

scientific_limitations: Classifies only ω(n)<=2; n=270 has three supports and integral H5, so theorem cannot be generalized without new work.
